data.title: Dark Mode
data.tagline: Dark mode is a switchable dark interface theme state, not merely a page with a black background.
data.learningOutcome: You can check that dark mode covers important interface states and contrast instead of only checking whether the background became black.
data.description: When someone chooses dark mode or their system prefers it, backgrounds, text, borders, buttons, charts, and focus states need coordinated, sufficiently contrasting values. It serves different environments and preferences. A single dark poster or visual style is not automatically a switchable theme.

learning.assumes: You have used light and dark appearance switching in an app or operating system.
learning.outcome: You can check that dark mode covers important interface states and contrast instead of only checking whether the background became black.

distinctions.label: Dark tech style
distinctions.explanation: Dark Mode is a product theme that can be switched or follow the system. Dark UI is a visual style that consistently uses dark surfaces and technology-themed graphics.

explanation.title: Color relationships change together
explanation.text: When backgrounds become dark, body text, muted hints, borders, buttons, inputs, charts, and code blocks all need contrast and hierarchy checks. Reversing one background alone is insufficient.

explanation.title: Respect a person's preference
explanation.text: A product can use `prefers-color-scheme` as a default and offer an explicit switch that remembers a choice. Focus, hover, selected, and error states must remain distinguishable after switching.

data.boundary: Dark mode is not the same as a dark visual style. The latter can be a fixed artistic choice for one page; dark mode is a full set of interface states that corresponds to light mode and can follow system or user preference. It also does not guarantee lower power use on every device.

lessonPractice.title: After the team changes a page background to dark gray, input borders and error messages are almost invisible. What should happen next?

options.label: Audit text, borders, inputs, errors, focus, and charts for contrast and state in the dark theme—not only the background
options.feedback: Correct. Dark mode is a full interface state, so key actions and feedback must remain clear.

options.label: Make the background even blacker; no other colors need change
options.feedback: A darker background does not automatically make borders, feedback, and focus discernible and may reduce readability.

options.label: Hide error messages to make the dark page cleaner
options.feedback: Errors remain feedback needed to complete a task; deleting them does not solve contrast.

data.agentPrompt: Implement dark mode: use system `prefers-color-scheme` as a possible default and provide a user switch. Give background, text, borders, inputs, errors, focus, charts, and code blocks matching theme values. Then check default, hover, focus, and error states in both light and dark modes.
